dod_intent_evidence: DARPA SBIR Phase II 2023 ($1.5M, Bulletproof Code C/C++-to-Rust translation — SBIR abstract); site cites CDAO and Air Force Platform One 'awardable' assessments; May 2026 news shows a competitive position on the Army's $49M NCODE cybersecurity IDIQ.
score_evidence: '# TRL9 ... Deployed and Battle Tested' — readiness-level brag, though wrapped in genuinely operational framing → lab_language_intensity

Fluent deployment language throughout: 'deployable in sensitive air-gapped environments', 'Pre-canned policies for FDA, EU CRA, DoD, NIST', 'deployed by government entities... in SaaS, on-prem, private-cloud, and air-gapped environments' — they get it, which per calibration scores LOW → deployment_awareness_absence
No jobs data in pack — hiring_profile_skew set to exactly 10 per rule

DARPA Phase II product is still 'TRL 5 technology' being productized ('We aim to productize this Phase I capability into Bulletproof Code®, a TRL 9 product') on a 6-person team — that clock is the residual pressure → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: Bulletproof Code has no named path out of DARPA — and DARPA does not field anything
blind_spots.operator_reality: The Phase II abstract promises to lift a 'TRL 5' Rust-translation capability to TRL 9, but names no service program of record, prime, or transition partner; when the DARPA period of performance ends, a translation engine without a transition agreement joins the valley of death regardless of how fielded the SBOM product is.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The team's commercial SBOM traction (Tradewinds, Platform One) makes transition feel solved company-wide, but the DARPA product line has a different customer and a different acquisition path.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Code 13 Security (doing business as Dark Sky Technology) has developed a Technical Readiness Level (TRL) 5 technology to translate type-unsafe source and binary software into the type-safe language Rust.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Air-gapped deployment of a product whose value is fresh threat intelligence
blind_spots.operator_reality: A supply-chain risk platform inside an air-gapped enclave only knows the vulnerabilities and contributor intel it was carried in with; their language sells the air-gap but never the update logistics — data-diode or sneakernet refresh cadence, who carries it, and how stale intel is flagged. In a SCIF, last month's threat feed is a false sense of security.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Intel-community founders know enclaves exist, but a 6-person product team's language stays at 'you don't have to share anything with us' rather than sustainment mechanics.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Bulletproof Trust can deploy in air-gapped environments, so you don't have to share anything with us.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Six cleared people against an eight-firm $49M Army IDIQ plus SaaS/on-prem/air-gapped instances
blind_spots.operator_reality: An NCODE position only pays if you can staff task orders — on-site installs in classified spaces, instance-by-instance sustainment, and RMF evidence for every deployment model they advertise. With '100% US citizens, cleared or clearable' as the whole bench, one won task order can consume the company and stall the DARPA productization at the same time.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Winning marketplace assessments (CDAO, Platform One) proves awardability, not delivery capacity; capacity gaps only surface after award.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Bulletproof Trust is a 100% US owned and operated company developed by 100% US citizens, cleared or clearable.

opener_hook: Dark Sky's DARPA Phase II calls Bulletproof Code a TRL 5 capability being productized to TRL 9 — the public record shows the Army NCODE seat for the SBOM line, but no named transition path for the Rust-translation engine when the DARPA money stops.
what_they_do: Six-person Colorado firm selling Bulletproof Trust, an SBOM management and software supply-chain risk platform for defense and regulated industries, plus a DARPA-funded C/C++-to-Rust code translation product.
